ages4To6.discoveryText: Mercury is a small planet close to the Sun.
ages4To6.readAloudText: Mercury is the little world nearest our Sun.

choices.text: It is close to the Sun.

picture.label: It is close to the Sun.

choices.text: It is an icy moon.

picture.label: It is an icy moon.

quiz.correctFeedback: You found Mercury! It is the closest planet to the Sun.
quiz.retryFeedback: Almost. Try the clue with the bright Sun.

ages7To9.discoveryText: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun. It travels around the Sun quickly.

choices.text: It is the closest planet to the Sun.

picture.label: It is the closest planet to the Sun.

choices.text: It is famous for red rusty dust.

picture.label: It is famous for red rusty dust.

choices.text: It is an icy moon of Jupiter.

picture.label: It is an icy moon of Jupiter.

quiz.correctFeedback: Nice scan! Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun.
quiz.retryFeedback: Try the clue about where Mercury travels.
quiz.hint: Look for the clue that mentions the Sun.

ages10To12.discoveryText: Mercury is the innermost and smallest planet. Its short orbit takes about 88 Earth days.

choices.text: It is the innermost planet and has a short orbit.

picture.label: It is the innermost planet and has a short orbit.

choices.text: Iron oxidation makes its surface look red.

picture.label: Iron oxidation makes its surface look red.

choices.text: It is an ice-covered moon orbiting Jupiter.

picture.label: It is an ice-covered moon orbiting Jupiter.

quiz.correctFeedback: Correct. Mercury's position nearest the Sun gives it the shortest planetary orbit.
quiz.retryFeedback: Compare each object's location and orbit.
quiz.hint: Which planet travels around the Sun in about 88 Earth days?

ages4To6.discoveryText: Mars is called the red planet.
ages4To6.readAloudText: Mars looks red because its dusty ground has rusty iron.

quiz.prompt: Which color clue belongs to Mars?

choices.text: Red and rusty

picture.label: Red and rusty

choices.text: White and icy

picture.label: White and icy

quiz.correctFeedback: Great exploring! Rusty dust makes Mars look red.
quiz.hint: Mars is called the red planet.

ages7To9.discoveryText: Mars looks red because rusty iron is mixed into its rocks, soil, and dust.

quiz.prompt: Why does Mars look red from far away?

choices.text: Rusty iron is mixed into its dust.

picture.label: Rusty iron is mixed into its dust.

choices.text: It is covered in red plants.

picture.label: It is covered in red plants.

choices.text: Jupiter shines red light on it.

picture.label: Jupiter shines red light on it.

quiz.correctFeedback: Great detective work! Rusty iron in the dust gives Mars its red color.
quiz.retryFeedback: Try the answer that matches the dust clue.

ages10To12.discoveryText: Iron minerals in Martian rocks and soil oxidize. This rusting process gives much of the surface its reddish color.

quiz.prompt: Which process best explains Mars's reddish surface?

choices.text: Iron-bearing minerals oxidize in the soil and dust.

picture.label: Iron-bearing minerals oxidize in the soil and dust.

choices.text: Seasonal vegetation changes the surface color.

picture.label: Seasonal vegetation changes the surface color.

choices.text: Red light reflected from Jupiter colors the surface.

picture.label: Red light reflected from Jupiter colors the surface.

quiz.correctFeedback: Exactly. Oxidation of iron-bearing minerals produces the rusty color.
quiz.retryFeedback: Look for a process involving iron and oxygen.
quiz.hint: Oxidation is the chemical process we commonly call rusting.

ages4To6.discoveryText: Europa is an icy moon that goes around Jupiter.
ages4To6.readAloudText: Europa is a shiny ice moon. An ocean may hide under its ice.

quiz.prompt: What kind of world is Europa?

choices.text: An icy moon

picture.label: An icy moon

choices.text: A red planet

picture.label: A red planet

quiz.correctFeedback: Excellent! Europa is one of Jupiter's icy moons.
quiz.retryFeedback: Try the world covered with ice.

ages7To9.discoveryText: Europa is an icy moon of Jupiter. Evidence suggests a salty ocean may exist beneath its ice.

quiz.prompt: What kind of world is Europa?

choices.text: An icy moon of Jupiter

picture.label: An icy moon of Jupiter

choices.text: The smallest planet near the Sun

picture.label: The smallest planet near the Sun

choices.text: A red planet with rusty dust

picture.label: A red planet with rusty dust

quiz.correctFeedback: Excellent explorer! Europa is Jupiter's icy moon.
quiz.retryFeedback: Try the clue that says Europa is a moon, not a planet.

ages10To12.discoveryText: Europa's young icy surface and magnetic measurements provide evidence for a global salty ocean beneath its shell.

choices.text: An icy Jovian moon with evidence for a subsurface ocean

picture.label: An icy Jovian moon with evidence for a subsurface ocean

choices.text: An inner planet with the shortest orbit around the Sun

picture.label: An inner planet with the shortest orbit around the Sun

choices.text: A planet colored by oxidized iron-rich dust

picture.label: A planet colored by oxidized iron-rich dust

quiz.correctFeedback: Correct. Multiple observations support the model of a salty ocean beneath Europa's ice.
quiz.retryFeedback: Separate the planet clues from the moon-and-ocean evidence.
quiz.hint: Europa orbits Jupiter, and its icy shell may cover liquid water.
